diagnostics.message: aws_lambda_function.pool should depend on aws_iam_role_policy.pool: the function is created as soon as the execution role exists, before the role's inline policy is attached and propagated, so early invocations can fail with access-denied errors. The function has no attribute referencing the policy, so a bare depends_on is required.

aws_lambda_function.pool should depend on aws_iam_role_policy.pool_logging: the logging policy (referencing aws_cloudwatch_log_group.pool.arn) must be attached to the execution role before the function can write logs; the function is created before the policy due to IAM propagation delays. No attribute reference can express this; a bare depends_on is required.

aws_lambda_function.pool should depend on aws_iam_role_policy.pool_xray: when tracing is enabled the function uses X-Ray, but the xray-policy may not yet be attached/propagated when the function is created, causing tracing setup failures on first invocation. A bare depends_on is required since no attribute of the function references the policy.

aws_lambda_function.pool should depend on aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.pool_vpc_execution_role (when VPC config is used): without the AWSLambdaVPCAccessExecutionRole attached and propagated, the function cannot create ENIs in the configured subnets and creation/invocation fails. No attribute of the function references the attachment, so a bare depends_on is required.

aws_lambda_function.pool should depend on aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.ami_id_ssm_parameter_read (when ami_id_ssm_parameter_name is set): the function reads the AMI id from SSM Parameter Store at invocation time, but the read policy may not be attached/propagated when the function is created. No attribute of the function references the attachment, so a bare depends_on is required.

aws_scheduler_schedule.pool should depend on aws_iam_role_policy.scheduler: the schedule's target role (aws_iam_role.scheduler) is referenced via role_arn, but the role's terraform policy granting lambda:InvokeFunction on aws_lambda_function.pool.arn may not be attached and propagated when the schedule fires, so early invocations fail with AccessDenied. No attribute of the schedule references the policy, so a bare depends_on is required.

aws_lambda_function.pool should be created after aws_cloudwatch_log_group.pool: the log group (/aws/lambda/<function_name>) must exist before the function so Lambda does not auto-create a default log group on first invocation (which would conflict with the Terraform-managed group and drop the configured retention/KMS settings). Note the current graph has the reverse edge (the log group references function_name), so adding a bare depends_on would cycle — the function name should be computed as a local used by both resources instead.
